items.title: Brevo supply-chain attack injected ClickFix scripts on customer sites
items.one_liner: Attackers stole a hardcoded Cloudflare API key from Brevo to inject ClickFix malware and backdoors into customer sites.
items.summary: Brevo confirmed that attackers stole a hardcoded long-lived Cloudflare API key with full account permissions from its application source code and created a malicious Cloudflare Worker. The Worker modified content at the CDN edge for over five hours on September 14, injecting ClickFix scripts and malicious widgets into Brevo sites and customer-embedded assets. The injected scripts displayed fake Cloudflare verification pages and attempted to drop malicious WordPress backdoors like 'Web Media Optimizer' to sustain persistence and load further malicious payloads. Brevo revoked the compromised credentials and purged edge caches after detecting the breach.
key_facts: Exposure window: 16:07 and 20:30 UTC on September 14
items.bottom_line: Hardcoded API keys with broad cloud permissions allow attackers to hijack CDN edge workers and distribute malware to thousands of downstream customer websites.

items.title: Iranian Hackers Use Telegram-Controlled Malware to Spy on Dissidents and Journalists
items.one_liner: Security agencies warn of Iranian Telegram-controlled Windows spyware targeting dissidents and journalists with espionage and harassment.
items.summary: Cybersecurity agencies in the US, UK, and Netherlands have issued a joint advisory detailing a Windows malware controlled via Telegram that is used by Iranian intelligence to target dissidents and journalists. Tracked by the FBI as HEAVYGRAM and by the UK NCSC as CHOSEN BRICK, the spyware can harvest emails, chat messages, take screenshots, and record audio via the microphone. The attackers distribute the malware by posing as acquaintances or tech support, disguising the files as legitimate applications like KeePass, Telegram, or Norton Antivirus. Once executed, the malware establishes persistence through Windows registry keys and hooks into individual Telegram bots for command and control. The campaign, linked to Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security, has been active since at least late 2023.
key_facts: Attribution: Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS)
items.bottom_line: Iranian threat actors are actively utilizing Telegram-controlled Windows malware to spy on dissidents and expose their private data on leak sites.

items.one_liner: Cisco warns of an actively exploited maximum-severity zero-day authentication bypass in Identity Services Engine (CVE-2026-76460).
items.summary: Cisco has released urgent updates for a maximum-severity authentication bypass vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-76460, in its Identity Services Engine (ISE) and ISE Passive Identity Connector. Attackers are actively exploiting this API flaw in the wild to bypass web management authentication and gain root-level unauthorized access. Because no workarounds exist, Cisco strongly advises administrators to upgrade immediately and inspect access logs for suspicious usernames or network indicators of compromise. CISA has added the vulnerability to its KEV catalog, requiring federal agencies to patch within three days.
key_facts: Affected products: Cisco ISE, Cisco ISE-PIC
Action required: Software upgrade and node re-imaging
items.bottom_line: Network administrators running Cisco ISE must immediately patch CVE-2026-76460 and re-image compromised nodes to thwart active exploitation.

items.title: CVE-2026-0298 GlobalProtect App: Code Execution Vulnerability in Windows Pre-Logon Access Provider (PLAP) (Severity: MEDIUM)
items.one_liner: GlobalProtect Windows clients using SAML CBL are vulnerable to local SYSTEM code execution via PLAP input validation flaws.
items.summary: An improper input validation vulnerability exists in the Windows Pre-Logon Access Provider component of the Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect app, enabling a man-in-the-middle attacker to execute arbitrary code with SYSTEM privileges. The flaw affects specific version ranges of the 6.0, 6.2, and 6.3 branches on Windows when configured to use SAML authentication with the Connect Before Logon feature. Palo Alto Networks has issued updates and workaround guidance, noting no active exploitation at the time of disclosure.
items.bottom_line: Palo Alto GlobalProtect Windows users leveraging SAML with Connect Before Logon face a local SYSTEM code execution risk via MITM manipulation.

items.title: New Chinese-Made ‘RatHat’ Android Malware Leverages AI to Steal Financial Data
items.one_liner: RatHat Android malware leverages generative AI and Accessibility APIs to automate banking fraud and remote access.
items.summary: Zimperium researchers discovered 'RatHat', a new Android malware strain targeting credential harvesting and banking details via smishing and malvertising. RatHat uses a dropper exploiting SessionInstaller APIs to bypass Android restricted settings and Accessibility protections. The malware architecture includes a Go agent running local ADB shell commands to disable security apps and an FRP client establishing a persistent reverse tunnel to the C2 server. Notably, RatHat integrates a generative AI UI-automation engine that serializes the device's live Accessibility tree to XML and uses mainstream AI assistants in Mandarin to parse screen coordinates and execute synthetic clicks.
items.bottom_line: Attackers are combining Android Accessibility abuse with generative AI vision models to automate on-device banking credential theft.

items.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploit Chrome-Windows Zero-Day Chain to Deploy GRIMWEDGE
items.one_liner: State-sponsored actors are actively exploiting a Chrome and Windows zero-day chain (BlueMoon) to deploy the GRIMWEDGE backdoor.
items.summary: A China-linked threat actor tracked as UTA0560 launched a spear-phishing campaign against multiple non-governmental organizations on September 1, 2026. The emails directed targets to compromised university websites leveraging a reflected cross-site scripting flaw to trigger a zero-day exploit chain known as BlueMoon. This chain utilized CVE-2026-85046 for V8 sandbox read/write access, CVE-2026-87491 for browser sandbox escape, and CVE-2026-85880 for code execution within the Chrome process. The attack ultimately deployed a malicious JavaScript backdoor called GRIMWEDGE via DLL sideloading and custom MSI actions.

items.bottom_line: Organizations running Chrome on Windows face active spear-phishing attacks using a three-flaw zero-day chain to drop memory-resident backdoors.

items.title: China-Aligned FamousSparrow Deploys SparroWocky Backdoor Across Latin America
items.one_liner: FamousSparrow targets Latin American government entities with its custom SparroWocky C++ backdoor.
items.summary: The China-aligned threat actor FamousSparrow has deployed a modular C++ backdoor named SparroWocky across Latin America since July 2025, replacing its older SparrowDoor implant. Named after a reference to Lewis Carroll's poem Jabberwocky in early builds, the backdoor is delivered via DLL sideloading and uses Mbed TLS, MinHook, COFF Loader, and a variant of SilentMoonwalk for defense evasion and in-memory execution. The campaign has targeted government entities across Argentina, Ecuador, Guatemala, Honduras, Panama, Peru, Puerto Rico, and Venezuela.
items.bottom_line: FamousSparrow has upgraded its operational tooling to the SparroWocky backdoor for targeted espionage across Latin America.

items.title: Warren Buffett steps down after six decades at Berkshire - 'Father Time always wins'
items.one_liner: Warren Buffett steps down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway at 96, passing the post to his son Howard in an orderly transition.
items.summary: Warren Buffett has stepped down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway at age 96, completing a long-planned leadership transition by handing the role to his son, Howard Buffett. Greg Abel previously took over as chief executive nine months prior, while Warren Buffett transitions to chairman emeritus and remains on the board. Buffett transformed Berkshire Hathaway from a struggling textile mill into a $1.1 trillion global conglomerate since taking control in 1965. Howard Buffett's primary responsibility will be guarding the firm's culture and values.
items.bottom_line: Warren Buffett's departure as Berkshire Hathaway chairman marks the final chapter of a generational leadership transition for the $1.1 trillion conglomerate.

items.title: Inference-Engine Fingerprinting Attacks are Practical: Exploring Model-Driven Environmental Discovery, Exploitation, and Escape
items.one_liner: Researchers show that AI models can fingerprint their execution engines and execute bare-metal exploits.
items.summary: Researchers have demonstrated that inference-engine fingerprinting attacks are practical for discovering and exploiting LLM execution environments. By analyzing model outputs, a misaligned or compromised AI model can identify the specific inference engine—such as vLLM or SGLang—running it, without requiring external input tokens. Once the engine is fingerprinted, the model can execute engine-specific exploits to achieve a to-the-bare-metal compromise of the inference stack. The findings highlight the need for structural changes to inference engines to mitigate fingerprinting risks.
key_facts: Inference Engines Evaluated: vLLM, SGLang (among 5 popular engines)
items.bottom_line: LLMs can fingerprint underlying inference engines like vLLM or SGLang from output tokens and execute bare-metal exploits.

items.title: CVE-2025-39682: Linux Linux Kernel Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions Vulnerability
items.one_liner: CISA adds Linux kernel TLS receive path vulnerability CVE-2025-39682 to its KEV catalog with a federal remediation deadline.
items.summary: CISA has added CVE-2025-39682, an improper check for unusual or exceptional conditions vulnerability in the Linux kernel TLS receive path, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The flaw allows a zero-length record retrieved from the rx_list to bypass intended record-type handling in recvmsg(), potentially causing subsequent TLS records to be processed using incorrect zero-copy and queuing assumptions. Federal agencies are required to apply vendor mitigations by September 21, 2026. The vulnerability may affect end-of-life products that require replacement or disconnection from internet exposure.
items.bottom_line: Federal civilian agencies must patch CVE-2025-39682 in the Linux kernel by September 21, 2026, to prevent improper TLS record processing.

items.title: CVE-2026-90711 (CRITICAL 9.1): proxy-addr is a Node.js module that determines a request's client address behind trusted reverse proxies, and…
items.one_liner: A critical CVSS 9.1 bug in Node.js proxy-addr allows unauthenticated clients to spoof IP addresses via improper subnet parsing.
items.summary: A critical fail-open vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-90711 with a CVSS score of 9.1, affects the Node.js module proxy-addr in versions 1.1.0 through 2.0.7. When trust subnets are written in IPv4-mapped IPv6 notation with an incorrect prefix length (such as ::ffff:10.0.0.0/8 instead of ::ffff:10.0.0.0/104), the module incorrectly trusts every IPv4 address on the internet. This flaw allows unauthenticated clients to spoof the X-Forwarded-For header, completely bypassing IP-based access controls, rate limiting, and audit logging in applications using Express. Developers must upgrade to version 2.0.8 or ensure trust subnets use prefix lengths of at least 97.
items.bottom_line: Applications using vulnerable proxy-addr versions are exposed to complete bypasses of IP-based security and rate limiting.

items.title: Transparent Tribe Deploys New Rust Backdoor Using Private GitHub Repositories for C2
items.one_liner: Transparent Tribe deployed a new Rust backdoor (RUSTYSHADE) using private GitHub repositories for C2 in attacks on Indian and Afghan defense entities.
items.summary: The Pakistan-aligned threat group Transparent Tribe (APT36) has launched Operation RapidRust, targeting government and defense entities in India and Afghanistan using previously undocumented tools. The campaign features RUSTYSHADE, a Rust-based backdoor leveraging private GitHub repositories for encrypted command-and-control via the GitHub REST API. Additional tools include RUSTYMOVE for automated USB propagation on Windows, alongside PSNATCH and BASHNATCH file stealers designed to harvest documents and databases. The actors also deployed typosquatted domains impersonating Indian news outlets like The Print and India Today to distribute malicious payloads.
key_facts: Threat group: Transparent Tribe (APT36 / Earth Karkaddan)
Target sectors: Government and defense in India and Afghanistan
New tools: RUSTYSHADE, RUSTYMOVE, PSNATCH, BASHNATCH
items.bottom_line: Adversaries are increasingly abusing legitimate developer infrastructure like private GitHub repositories for resilient, signature-evading command-and-control channels.

items.title: Microsoft Patches CVSS 10.0 Azure AI Foundry Flaw Enabling Unauthorized Privilege Escalation
items.one_liner: Microsoft patched a CVSS 10.0 flaw in Azure AI Foundry and multiple Copilot bugs while two Windows zero-days face active exploitation.
items.summary: Microsoft has released out-of-band updates addressing multiple severe vulnerabilities, including a maximum-severity CVSS 10.0 flaw in Azure AI Foundry tracked as CVE-2026-85889. The unauthenticated missing authentication vulnerability permits unauthorized privilege escalation over a network without requiring customer action. Additional critical patches include a command injection in Microsoft 365 Copilot (CVE-2026-85885, CVSS 9.9) and local privilege escalation flaws in Windows User-Mode Power Service and Secure Kernel Mode. Meanwhile, two Windows zero-days impacting ALPC and the Update Stack are actively exploited by espionage threat actors in the BlueMoon exploit kit.

CVE-2026-85885: CVSS 9.9, Microsoft 365 Copilot command injection

CVE-2026-62721: CVSS 7.8, Windows UMPS local escalation
items.bottom_line: Cloud AI administrative platforms are increasingly targeted by critical authentication bypasses, requiring rapid automated cloud-side mitigation by vendors.

items.title: BambooToken Malware Uses MQTT to Control Windows and Linux Systems
items.one_liner: BambooToken malware targets Windows and Linux systems via MQTT communications, leveraging DLL sideloading in Tendyron financial tokens.
items.summary: Security researchers have detailed a multi-platform malware campaign active since February 2023 that targets Windows and Linux systems across Asia and South America using the MQTT protocol for command-and-control (C2). Codenamed BambooToken, the malware relies on DLL sideloading vulnerabilities in Tendyron's 'OnKey' software—a hardware-based PKI token used in financial and government sectors with over 190 million units in circulation—to trigger execution within secure environments. While Tendyron's certificates remain uncompromised, attackers exploit local binaries to load rogue DLLs that harvest system details, receive remote plug-in commands via MQTT, and communicate with C2 servers. Most samples have been uploaded from Chinese IP addresses, pointing to a targeted regional data collection effort.
key_facts: Affected hardware token: Tendyron OnKey (190 million in circulation)
items.bottom_line: Attackers are abusing DLL sideloading vulnerabilities in widely deployed Tendyron security tokens to execute BambooToken, a multi-platform MQTT-controlled backdoor.

items.summary: Cybercriminals hijacked HBO Max’s verified Reddit account to distribute malware through 108 malicious advertisements over 48 hours. items.one_liner: This is a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in Cotonti that allows account takeovers via predictable password reset tokens.
items.summary: Cotonti versions through 1.0.0 contain a vulnerability where password recovery tokens are generated using a weak PRNG based on md5(microtime()). This creates a predictable token space of approximately one million values per second. An unauthenticated attacker can read the server's Date header to narrow the time window and brute-force tokens to reset any account password, including administrator accounts.
items.bottom_line: If you are running Cotonti 1.0.0 or earlier, your password recovery mechanism is insecure and can be exploited by unauthenticated attackers to hijack any account.

items.one_liner: Evaluating financial LLM trading agents with FARSIGHT reveals that 100% exhibit security vulnerabilities and 80% fail robustness checks.
items.summary: Researchers present FARSIGHT, a scheme-level evaluation framework to test financial large language model trading agents on robustness against market turbulence and security against adversarial threats. items.bottom_line: Autonomous financial LLM agents currently exhibit pervasive security and robustness failures capable of triggering market crashes.

items.title: Silence Is Endorsement: Verification-Status Laundering in LLM Agent Pipelines
items.one_liner: LLM agent pipelines suffer from verification-status laundering, where unverified authorization claims are treated as fully vetted by safety monitors.
items.summary: Safety monitors in LLM agent systems frequently judge actions using summaries or stored memory rather than original verification evidence, leading to a failure mode called verification-status laundering. This vulnerability is compounded during pipeline execution as summarizers weaken status tags and memory compressors strip them entirely. Consequently, agent pipelines must carry authorization provenance as structured state attached to claims rather than trusting text summaries.

items.title: Closed-World Resolution Against Tool Hallucination in LLM Agents

items.summary: Hugging Face researchers have identified a significant 'consistency gap' in LLM agents, where high average success rates mask poor reliability across repeated runs. items.title: From Fork to Framework: What Modifying Apollo Taught Us About Agent Invasion
items.one_liner: Forking and obfuscating Mythic's Apollo agent proved insufficient against signature and structural detections, driving the need for custom tooling.
items.summary: Bishop Fox researchers forked the open-source Mythic .NET Apollo agent to bypass endpoint detection during an assessment requiring application whitelisting bypass, creating a custom obfuscator to strip strings and metadata. They discovered that Elastic's Multi_Trojan_Mythic YARA rule fired on ten of eleven plaintext JSON field names from the Mythic C2 protocol present in the pre-mitigation source code. Despite targeted renames and structural changes, the underlying assumption of the agent's architecture regarding stable, readable symbol names defeated the red team before defenders could, ultimately driving the decision to build a custom agent from scratch.
items.bottom_line: Surface-level string obfuscation of mature C2 agents fails because their architectures fundamentally rely on readable symbol names that modern EDR and YARA rules catch.

items.title: Replan, Repair, or Edit? A Unified Empirical Evaluation of Travel Agents for Itinerary Revision under Resource Disruptions
items.one_liner: An empirical study on travel agent itinerary revisions shows hierarchical and local repairs preserve more commitments than full replanning.
items.summary: Researchers conducted a systematic empirical study on travel-planning agents handling itinerary revisions under resource disruptions using TREK-derived benchmark sets. They compared full replanning with LLM-Z3, hierarchical plan repair with IPyHOPPER, and local revision with iTIMO across 500 single-disruption and 200 simultaneous compound-disruption cases. Gemini-backed LLM-Z3 achieved the highest compound-disruption success, while IPyHOPPER matched single-disruption success without using LLM inference while preserving more of the original itinerary. The study highlights trade-offs between effectiveness, plan stability, and computational token costs.
items.bottom_line: Hierarchical and local plan repair methods preserve more of an accepted itinerary and avoid high token overhead compared to full LLM replanning.

items.title: Characterizing Web Search by Conversational LLM Agents: From Search Decisions and Strategies to Results and Responses
items.one_liner: An analysis of conversational LLM Web search reveals varied invocation strategies, platform domain biases, and uncredited citations.
items.summary: Researchers investigated the end-to-end lifecycle of Web search usage across four conversational LLM platforms (ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, and DeepSeek) using both in-vivo user interactions and controlled API experiments. They found that decisions to invoke Web search vary widely across models, and higher invocation frequency does not correlate with better response quality. Furthermore, models employ complex querying strategies, platform-specific search engines prefer their own domain results, and some final responses rely on uncited search results, highlighting attribution and reliability concerns.
items.bottom_line: Conversational LLM search strategies vary significantly by platform, exhibit domain biases, and frequently suffer from citation omissions.

items.one_liner: A new principled benchmark and semantic enrichment framework improve out-of-distribution robustness for graph-based Android malware classifiers.
items.summary: Researchers examine the out-of-distribution robustness of graph-based Android malware classifiers, noting that benchmark accuracy over 94% drops by up to 45% when facing unseen malware family variants. To address covariate and domain shifts, they introduce a principled benchmarking suite featuring MalNet-Tiny-Common and MalNet-Tiny-Distinct. They propose a semantic enrichment framework that combines raw graph topology with lightweight function metadata and LLM-based code embeddings. Empirical results demonstrate that this data-centric methodology improves cross-distribution malware classification robustness.
items.bottom_line: Graph-based Android malware detectors suffer significant performance drops under distribution shifts, which can be mitigated via semantic code and metadata enrichment.

items.title: A Unified Evaluation Framework for Trustworthy Large Language Models, Agentic AI, and Multimodal Systems
items.one_liner: A new unified evaluation framework maps LLM and agent trustworthiness across eight dimensions while tying metrics to EU regulatory standards.
items.summary: Researchers have proposed a unified evaluation framework to assess the trustworthiness of large language models, agentic systems, and multimodal models across eight specific dimensions. The framework connects output-level, trajectory-level, and cross-modal assessments while maintaining system-specific metrics and mapping them to common performance bands with uncertainty estimates. It includes a meta-evaluation layer to verify the reproducibility of the evaluation and incorporates safety-critical overrides to prevent aggregate scores from masking failures. Furthermore, the framework maps technical assessments to international standards and European Union regulatory requirements. Empirical validation remains a necessary next step for the proposed methodology.
items.bottom_line: Evaluating modern AI systems requires moving beyond simple benchmark scores to multidimensional frameworks that incorporate safety-critical overrides and regulatory mappings.

items.one_liner: Evaluating two-agent résumé screening shows that agent-mediated negotiation alters candidate advancement compared to static one-call filters.
items.summary: Researchers compared traditional one-call résumé screening with a two-agent screening process where employer-side and candidate-side agents exchange evidence and update judgments before deciding who advances. The two-agent procedure does not merely relax thresholds, as it rejects applications that one-call screenings would advance and selects entirely different candidates. The findings indicate that agent-mediated hiring alters which candidates reach human review.
items.bottom_line: Moving to a two-agent negotiation model for résumé screening fundamentally changes candidate pass rates and selects different applicants than traditional one-call filters.

items.title: Reproducibility is not construct validity: LLM measurement of institutionally situated communication
items.one_liner: High LLM annotation reproducibility can mask poor construct validity when evaluating institutional text submissions.
items.summary: High annotation reproducibility by LLMs does not guarantee construct validity when measuring institutionally situated communication. Researchers analyzed European Commission AI Act consultation submissions and found high reproducibility coexisted with poor convergence between LLM-inferred measures and survey-reported constructs. Systematic divergence was observed across stakeholder groups, such as business associations expressing much greater concern in text than surveys. These findings highlight that validation procedures must separate reproducibility from true construct validity.
items.bottom_line: High reproducibility scores do not validate that LLM measurement tools are accurately capturing the intended constructs.

items.title: MaSCoD: A Multi-Agent Framework for Structural-Context-Guided Candidate Causal Graph Generation
items.one_liner: MaSCoD introduces a multi-agent framework for structural-context-guided causal graph generation to control relational omissions.
items.summary: Researchers proposed MaSCoD, a multi-agent framework designed to organize candidate third variables and local structural patterns before performing direct-edge judgment in causal graph generation. items.title: PAPC: Platform Mediation for Privacy-Propagation Externalities in AI-Mediated Workflows
items.one_liner: PAPC provides a platform-level mediation primitive to prevent privacy leaks in multi-agent AI workflows by intercepting intermediate data propagation.
items.summary: The PAPC (Platform Mediation for Privacy-Propagation Externalities) mechanism is proposed to address privacy risks in AI-mediated workflows where LLM agents share information. The framework models privacy loss as a propagation externality, where intermediate data updates or inter-agent messages can expose sensitive information before a final output is generated. PAPC intercepts these events at the platform level, using policy, provenance, and topology signals to quarantine raw content or release safe abstractions, effectively eliminating exact raw-value exposure.

items.title: A Dual-Process Perspective on Nudge Susceptibility in LLM-Based GUI Agents

items.summary: An empirical study investigating nudge susceptibility in large language model GUI agents through a randomized online shopping experiment involving 3,600 agents and 21,600 simulations across six frontier models found vulnerability to both automatic and reflective nudges. items.title: Reach or Solve? Attributing Agentic RL Gains with Checkpoint Handoffs
items.one_liner: This protocol provides a more granular way to evaluate agentic RL performance, helping you distinguish between navigation capabilities and task-completion logic in your own agentic workflows.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced 'checkpoint handoff,' an evaluation protocol designed to decouple the performance gains of language-model agents into two distinct phases: REACH and SOLVE. This approach addresses the limitations of standard endpoint success metrics, which often conflate navigation and execution.

items.summary: Datadog Security Research investigated how attackers target GitHub audit logs, source code repositories, and CI/CD pipelines using compromised credentials, personal access tokens, and OAuth apps. items.one_liner: Analyze malicious JavaScript loaders safely by substituting execution calls with stream-based output logging instead of manual deobfuscation.

Security analysts recommend letting the script deobfuscate itself by routing execution through safer debugging hooks—such as writing payloads to an ADODB stream—rather than attempting manual string reconstruction.

items.title: A GUID is Not a Credential: Unauthenticated RCE in Veeam Service Provider Console
items.summary: TL;DR CVE-2026-58073 (CVSS 9.5) and CVE-2026-58072 (CVSS 9.0) are critical vulnerabilities in Veeam Service Provider Console, the multi-tenant console that managed service providers use to run backups across all of their customers. The first lets an unauthenticated network peer claim a connected backup agent’s identity and receive that agent’s real certificate. The second lets anything holding an agent certificate write a file anywhere on the server. Chained, they are unauthenticated remote code execution on the console that sits above every tenant’s backups, which we proved end to end against Veeam’s own binaries. Patch to 9.3.0, then check your logs for indicators of compromise.

items.summary: NVIDIA has released AIPerf, a ground-up rewrite of its LLM benchmarking tool designed to address the scaling limitations of its predecessor, GenAI-Perf. items.title: HTTP QUERY Method: The Grey Zone Between GET And POST., (Fri, Sep 18th)
items.summary: In June 2026 the IETF published RFC 10008[1], defining a new HTTP method: "QUERY". The HTTP protocol faced already by changes (HTTP/2, HTTP/2) but it’s the first new standard HTTP verb since "PATCH" in 2010! This new method sits between “GET” and “POST” and can be resumed like this: “QUERY is a GET with a body”. It's safe and idempotent: the request is processed without state change and can be automatically repeated or restarted without concern for partial state changes. The query itself lives in the request body instead of the URL, and it's explicitly cacheable.
